findings.issue: The plan provisions discounts with `discountAutomaticBasicCreate` / `discountAutomaticBxgyCreate` (automatic discounts — no code, apply by rule) but then in `add-bundle-to-cart` instructs the coding agent to pass "discount code derived from the applicable tier's discount external id" to `cartCreate`. Automatic discounts have no customer-facing code; `cartCreate`'s `discountCodes` input accepts only code-based discounts. The discount will silently not apply at checkout — the core value proposition of the app is broken.
findings.fix: Replace `discountAutomaticBasicCreate` / `discountAutomaticBxgyCreate` with `discountCodeBasicCreate` / `discountCodeBxgyCreate` throughout the plan so that each tier produces a redeemable code that can be passed to `cartCreate`; update all matching update/activate/deactivate steps to their code-discount counterparts (`discountCodeBasicUpdate`, `discountCodeActivate`, `discountCodeDeactivate`).

findings.issue: Column `discount_value` is given role `ratio` with purpose "interpreted as a fraction for percentage, absolute amount for flat, or free-item count for buy-X-get-Y". The spec reserves `ratio` for values bounded 0–1. A flat-amount discount is a currency value (`money`) and a buy-X-get-Y free-item count is an integer (`count`); neither is bounded between 0 and 1. The coding agent will infer a single fractional column and will mishandle both the flat-amount and buy-X-get-Y cases.
findings.fix: Split `discount_value` into two nullable columns: `discount_value_ratio` (role `ratio`, used for percentage tiers) and `discount_value_amount` (role `money`, used for flat tiers); the buy-X-get-Y quantity is already captured by `minimum_item_count` and the bundle's `required_item_count`, so no additional column is needed — document this in the column purpose rather than overloading a single field.

findings.issue: Idempotency is declared as "if a purchase record already exists for this order external id, treat the event as a no-op", but `bundle_purchases` is keyed by `bundle_id + order_external_id`. If a retry fires after the first delivery recorded only some of the bundles in an order (e.g. the handler wrote bundle A then crashed before bundle B), the order-level guard will skip the entire event on retry and bundle B's purchase will never be recorded, corrupting `purchase_count`.
findings.fix: Change idempotency to "check per bundle_id + order_external_id; skip insertion only for the specific bundle+order pair that already has a record, so a partial-failure retry can still record the remaining bundles in the same order".

findings.issue: There is no admin GET route for a single bundle's full detail (title, type, item pool with positions and availability flags, tier list). The edit form served by `/admin/bundles/update` POST cannot be populated without first loading that data. The only admin GET declared is `/admin/bundles` whose responseShape is `bundles: list` — insufficient for an edit view that must pre-fill every field including nested items and tiers.
findings.fix: Add an admin GET `/admin/bundles/detail` with requestShape `{bundle_id: identifier}` and responseShape `{bundle: object, items: list, tiers: list}` so the edit UI can fetch the existing configuration before submitting changes.

findings.issue: Purpose states "the discount magnitude; interpreted as a fraction for percentage, absolute amount for flat, or free-item count for buy-X-get-Y" — embedding three mutually exclusive interpretations in one column's purpose string is the smell that reveals the type-overloading bug (see finding 2 above), and it also means the coding agent has no unambiguous rule for which interpretation to apply at runtime without reading the parent bundle's `discount_kind`.
findings.fix: After splitting into `discount_value_ratio` and `discount_value_amount` per finding 2, give each column a single-interpretation purpose (e.g. "fraction of the bundle total discounted, used when discount kind is percentage") so the coding agent can apply each without a conditional lookup.
